newsitem.title: UK: Eurostar UK owner hopes for share float in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Eurostar UK owner hopes for share float in 1998.

text.p: The London and Continental Railways (L&CR) consortium which owns the Eurostar (UK) Channel Tunnel passenger train service hopes to go public with a share flotation in 1998, a company executive said on Wednesday.

L&CR has previously said it hoped to float in late 1997 as part of its financing strategy for its three billion stg project to build and operate a new fast railway between London and the Channel Tunnel which is due to be ready by the year 2003.

But business development director Theo Steel told Reuters the likely timing was now "some time in 1998" because it formally took over Eurostar (UK) from the British government four months later than expected in June this year.
The consortium of banking, construction and travel firms was given Eurostar, along with a 999 year operating concession, as the price for taking on the fast rail link project.
L&CR is now racing to boost traffic and turn Eurostar (UK) into a profitable business to attract public investors.
On Wednesday Eurostar (UK) launched a Frequent Traveller departure lounge at London Waterloo station.

Eurostar says demand is currently running at a rate of 6.4 million passengers a year, up from around 3.9 million passengers a year ago. Steel said growth was running to plan with break-even point likely to be around the 10 million mark, depending on average fare yields.
Current capacity is about 15 million passengers a year, the company said.

L&CR shareholders include bus transport firm National Express, British entrepreneur Richard Branson's airline to retail conglomerate Virgin Group, investment bank SBC Warburg, U.S. project management specialist Bechtel and civil engineering consultants Ove Arup and Halcrow.
